text:
maria: heads-up — found a mutating webhook in staging that is creating a RoleBinding against the deployer service account with cluster-admin-like perms for 12h. saw it in audit logs around 10:12 UTC.
aj: 😬 which webhook? name/path?
maria: webhook is `image-injector.redwood.svc` — it patches pods on create. the patch includes an annotation that our infra reconciler picks up and then creates a RoleBinding. suspect the annotation processing code mis-parses the namespace and uses cluster role instead of namespaced role.
devon: do you have the exact audit entry? can you paste the snippet?
maria: pasted below:
```
{"kind":"RoleBinding","apiVersion":"rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1","metadata":{"name":"deployer-binding-xyz","namespace":"staging"},"roleRef":{"apiGroup":"rbac.authorization.k8s.io","kind":"ClusterRole","name":"cluster-admin"},"subjects":[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"deployer-sa","namespace":"staging"}]}
```
kevin: that roleRef is definitely wrong for a namespaced binding. code should have used Role not ClusterRole. which reconciler creates the binding?
maria: infra-reconciler v2.3.1 — the code path is annotator -> bind-controller. bind-controller reads `rbac.redwood/role: deployer` annotation and escalates.
lia: quick question — is this limited to staging? any signs in prod?
maria: only saw it in staging so far. checked prod audit-logs for the same pattern and nothing. but the reconciler version is rolling to canary next hour, so we might hit prod soon.
security-bot: ALERT: potential privilege escalation pattern detected for serviceAccount=deployer-sa namespace=staging roleRef=cluster-admin. Suggested action: pause reconciler rollout, rotate SA keys, audit last 48h.
aj: pause the rollout now. @devon can you open a quick PR to pin reconciler to v2.3.0 in canary?
devon: on it. also adding a guard in bind-controller to reject ClusterRole refs when creating a namespaced RoleBinding.
kevin: we should also add an admission check to block creation of RoleBinding with ClusterRole in the same namespace — double protection.
lia: filesystem forensics — any evidence the deployer-SA tokens were used externally?
maria: looked at kube-apiserver audit: no Create/Exec as deployer-sa observed except normal CI jobs. token last-used is 10:21 UTC for a CI pod — leaving as precaution to rotate.
sre-bot: action items created: #1234 pause-release, #1235 rotate-deployer-sa, #1236 add-admission-policy, #1237 patch-bind-controller. ETA 60m.
devon: adding logging to bind-controller and a safe-mode that refuses to create roleBindings referencing ClusterRole unless explicit env var ENABLE_CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING=true is set by ops. will push a patch now.
aj: good. also add unit test for parsing annotation where namespace can be empty or `""` — that was the bug in an older rollout.
kevin: for the medium-term, we need an audit alert rule: any RoleBinding created with roleRef.kind==ClusterRole should emit high-severity alert if subject.namespace is set. lia can you draft that SIEM rule?
lia: yup will draft and sync with security-sig in 30m.
maria: rotating SA now — will also revoke any tokens issued via tokenrequest API after 10:10 UTC. posting command: 
```
kubectl -n staging delete secret deployer-sa-token-*
kubectl -n staging create token deployer-sa --duration=1h | xargs -I{} echo rotated {}
```
security-bot: NOTE: remember to run `gcloud kms decrypt` audit on any exported secrets in the last 24h; flagging artifacts for review.
devon: patch pushed to hotfix branch, CI running. will hold canary update until approval.
aj: once CI passes, let's do a quick canary in non-prod only for 1 pod, watch audit logs for 15m, then proceed.
kevin: postmortem owner? maria you found it so seems fair. pls own and include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups.
maria: will own. initial page will be in /postmortems/bridge with incident id RWB-2026-045. drafting now.
lia: adding compliance checklist: KMS access review, token issuance logs, and proof of least-priv for bind-controller.
maria: thanks all — will update thread with PR links and timestamps. :thumbsup:
